recipes.name: 5 Weeknight Recipes for Pork Tenderloin
ingredients: 1 (1lb) pork tenderloin, cut into 1 inch cubes
1 lb pork tenderloin, cut into small strips
For the Sweet and Sour Sauce
1 large garlic clove, smashed and minced
1 small red bell pepper, large dice
1 small green bell pepper, large dice
1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
1/2 cup plus 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, divided
1/4 cup fresh juice from 2 lemons, divided
1 (6 oz) can tuna in olive oil, drained
instructions: For Pork Tenderloin Medallions with Bourbon Sauce:
For the Medallions
Begin by cutting the tenderloin into 2 even halves. - 1 lb pork tenderloin

Dry brine with a generous sprinkle of salt on all sides and let rest at room temperature for 45 minutes to 2 hours to improve flavor and moisture retention. - 1 lb pork tenderloin - kosher salt to taste
Once the pork has rested, thoroughly preheat a stainless steel pan over medium-high heat with vegetable oil until nearly smoking. - vegetable oil as needed

Transfer the dry-brined tenderloin halves to the preheated pan, making sure it’s coated in the oil, and pressing down to maximize contact. They should basically be sticking to the pan. - vegetable oil as needed - 1 lb pork tenderloin
Cook on one side for 2 to 3 minutes, or until a golden crust forms. Repeat on all 4 sides. - 1 lb pork tenderloin
If the kitchen becomes too smoky, transfer the entire pan w/ the tenderloin halves to a 300°F preheated oven and cook for about 20-25 minutes. - 1 lb pork tenderloin
The pork should reach 145°F at its thickest point. - 1 lb pork tenderloin
Remove the pork from the oven and pan, and wrap tightly in aluminum foil to finish cooking. - 1 lb pork tenderloin
While the pork is resting, make the sauce.
For the Pan Sauce
Mince the shallots. - ½ cup shallots minced
Make the Chicken Stock Slurry by combining the gelatin with a few tablespoons of the chicken stock, stirring until a jelly-like paste forms. - 1 packet gelatin - 1 cup chicken stock
In the same stainless steel pan, scrape up the fond from the pork and sauté the minced shallots for about 2-3 minutes, or until just translucent. - shallots minced
Then, remove from the flame completely and deglaze with bourbon. - ½ cup bourbon
Once the alcohol has burned off, add the chicken stock and the Chicken Stock Slurry. - chicken stock - gelatin
Bring to a simmer. Season to taste with freshly ground pepper and kosher salt. - freshly ground pepper to taste - kosher salt to taste
The sauce is finished when a spoon or whisk leaves a streak when running across the pan. Optionally add drippings from the rested pork. - pork drippings
Once finished, kill the heat and add heavy cream and whisk together. - ¼ cup heavy cream
Then add unsalted butter and whisk until completely combined. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
After the butter has completely melted, add Dijon mustard and whisk until homogenous. Taste and adjust for seasoning. - 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
For the Pork
Slice the rested pork into medallions. - For the Medallions

Serve hot with Bourbon Pan Sauce and garnish with parsley and tarragon. - Bourbon Pan Sauce - freshly chopped parsley to garnish - freshly chopped tarragon to garnish - For the Medallions - For the Bourbon Pan Sauce
For Pork Schnitzel (Fried Pork Cutlets):
For the Pork
Break down the tenderloin into wide, skinny cutlets, about 3 pieces. - 1 lb (1 lb) pork tenderloin

Then, butterfly each tenderloin cutlet the same way you would a chicken breast, slicing it from its thickest side almost all the way through. Then open the cutlet along the uncut seam like a book. - 1 (1 lb) pork tenderloin
Cover the butterflied cutlets with plastic wrap and then pound until thin (about ¼ to ½ inch thick) using a meat tenderizer. - 1 (1 lb) pork tenderloin
Dry brine by sprinkling with kosher salt and letting sit for 45 minutes in the fridge, uncovered. - 1 (1 lb) pork tenderloin - kosher salt

While the pork is resting, set up your breading station in 3 separate wide, shallow bowls, one bowl with all-purpose flour, one bowl with 2 beaten eggs, a pinch of salt and a splash of water, and the last bowl with Panko breadcrumbs. - 1 ½ cups flour - 2 eggs - 1 ½ cups plain breadcrumbs
Do not begin the breading process until your frying is preheated so the breaded, uncooked pork does not sit around for too long.
For the Frying
In a large, high-walled pan, preheat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil to 375°F.
Bread the dry-brined pork cutlets by first dredging in flour, then the egg mixture, and finally the Panko breadcrumbs. - flour - eggs - plain breadcrumbs - For the Pork
Cook each pork cutlet in the oil until golden brown, around 3-5 minutes. - For the Pork
Remove from the oil using a kitchen spider, and drain on a wire rack set over a rimmed baking sheet. - For the Pork
Sprinkle the cutlets with salt while they are still hot. - kosher salt - For the Pork
Serve hot with mashed potatoes, herbs, and cranberry sauce. - For the Pork
Mashed Potatoes Recipe Link: https://www.babi.sh/recipes/mashed-potatoes
Thanksgiving Sides Recipe Link: https://www.babi.sh/recipes/last-minute-thanksgiving
For Pork Souvlaki:
For the Pork
Begin by chopping the tenderloin into 1-inch or bite-sized pieces. - 1 (1lb) pork tenderloin cut into 1 inch cubes
Transfer the pork pieces to a glass bowl and season with kosher salt. - ½ tsp kosher salt - For the Pork
For the Marinade

In a small bowl, combine lemon juice, olive oil, dried oregano, honey, garlic cloves, and freshly ground black pepper. Whisk until homogenous. - large lemon juiced - 3 oz olive oil - 1 tbsp dried oregano - 1 tbsp honey - 2 garlic cloves minced - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
For the Pork
Add the marinade to the pork and mix until fully incorporated. - For the Pork - For the Marinade
Cover and refrigerate for at least an hour and up to 12. - For the Pork - For the Marinade
For the Grilling
Once the pork is marinated, transfer the Marinated Pork to 2 metal skewers making sure to leave a 2 ½ inch gap at the bottom of each skewer for easy handling. - For the Pork
Preheat your oven’s broiler.
Then, place the skewered pork on an aluminum-lined rimmed baking sheet. - For the Pork
Transfer to a preheated oven on the highest rack centered directly under the heating element. - For the Pork
Rotate the baking sheet once or twice during cooking.

Meanwhile, make the Souvlaki spice mixture. In a small bowl, add the oregano, thyme, garlic powder, kosher salt, and freshly ground pepper. Reserve until ready to use. - 1 tbsp dried oregano - 1 tsp dried thyme - ½ tsp garlic powder - ½ tsp kosher salt - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper

When the pork is brown on 1 side, remove from the oven and flip, using the skewers. The pork should be cooked all the way through, but to double check, its thickest point should register between 145°F and 150°F. - For the Pork

Once completely cooked, drizzle with fresh lemon juice, sprinkle with the Soulvaki spice mixture, and serve hot with rice pilaf and a tomato cucumber salad. - large lemon juiced - For the Souvlaki Spice Mix - rice pilaf - tomato and cucumber Salad - For the Pork
For American Sweet & Sour Pork:
For the Pork
Begin by breaking down the pork into 1-inch or bite-sized pieces. - 1 lb pork tenderloin cut into small strips
Transfer to a glass bowl. - 1 lb pork tenderloin cut into small strips
For the Marinade
In a small bowl, add the vegetable oil, dark soy sauce, and corn starch, whisk until homogenous. - 1 tbsp vegetable oil - 1 tbsp light soy sauce - 1 tbsp cornstarch
Then, toss the pork in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 30 to 60 minutes. - 1 lb pork tenderloin cut into small strips
For the Sweet and Sour Sauce

Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, make the sweet and sour sauce. Combine white vinegar, light soy sauce, white sugar, worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, pineapple juice, ginger, and garlic. - ⅓ cup white vinegar - 1 tbsp light soy sauce - ⅓ cup sugar - 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce - 1 tsp oyster sauce - ¼ cup ketchup - ¼ cup pineapple juice - ½ inch ginger peeled and minced - 1 large garlic clove smashed and minced
Reserve ½ of the mixture and add cornstarch. Set aside. - 2 tbsp cornstarch - For the Sweet and Sour Sauce
For the Stir Fry
Preheat the wok over high heat until ripping hot with a table of vegetable oil. - 2 tbsp vegetable oil
While the wok is preheating, dice the vegetables. - For the Stir Fry
Add marinated pork and sear until just colored - this should take less than 30 seconds. The wok needs to be very hot. Stir constantly. - For the Pork
Once the pork is browned, add the diced vegetables. - 1 small yellow onion large dice - 1 small red bell pepper large dice - 1 small green bell pepper large dice
Toss the stir fry by hand or with the long-handled spoon, keeping the mixture moving.
Then, add pineapple and un-cornstarched half of the sauce. Stir and cook for 30 seconds. - 1 cup pineapple tidbits
After 30 seconds, use the cornstarched half of the sauce to adjust mixture’s thickness to your preference. - For the Sweet and Sour Sauce
For the Serving
Once the veggies are softened, the pork should be cooked through. - For the Pork - For the Sweet and Sour Sauce - For the Stir Fry

Serve immediately on a bed of steamed white rice, and garnish with sesame seeds and scallions. - 1 cup steamed white rice - sesame seeds to garnish - finely chopped scallions to garnish - For the Serving
For Pork Tenderloin Leftovers with Tonnato:
https://www.seriouseats.com/pork-tenderloin-vitello-tonnato-recipe

Place egg, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, mustard, capers, and anchovies in the bottom of an immersion blender cup. Pour remaining 1/2 cup vegetable oil on top and allow it to settle for 15 seconds. - 1 large whole egg - 2 tbsp fresh juice from 2 lemons divided - 1 tsp Dijon mustard - 1 tsp drained capers - 2 anchovy fillets - ½ cup plus 1 tablespoon vegetable oil divided
Place the head of the immersion blender at the bottom of the cup and switch it on. As mayonnaise forms, slowly tilt and lift the head of the immersion blender until all oil is emulsified.
Add tuna and remaining 2 tablespoons lemon juice and blend until thoroughly incorporated into a smooth sauce. - 1 (6 oz) can tuna in olive oil drained - 2 tbsp fresh juice from 2 lemons divided
Transfer mayonnaise to a large mixing bowl and slowly drizzle in 1/2 cup olive oil, whisking until emulsified. Season with salt and pepper. - ½ cup extra virgin olive oil plus more for drizzling

Slice pork very thinly against the grain. Arrange on a large plate and spoon tuna mayonnaise all over, spreading to form an even coating. You can refrigerate the pork tonnato, covered with plastic, for up to 8 hours; it will improve in flavor as it sits. - 1 cooked pork tenderloin chilled
When ready to serve, toss garnish with a small drizzle of olive oil and salt. Arrange on top and serve right away. - extra virgin olive oil plus more for drizzling - celery salad
